capabilities: Build light and dark colour systems with visual colour pickers
Preview changes live in a pocket-sized Obsidian preview
View and copy the generated theme.css beside the controls
Choose interface, reading, and code fonts from visual specimens
Export a named theme folder Obsidian can discover and update
disambiguation: Not a theme itself; it is a plugin that teaches theme creation and exports a standalone theme that works without the plugin.
extras: Not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; releases include signed build-provenance attestations and the plugin has no telemetry; development is supported via GitHub Sponsors and Buy Me a Coffee.
motivation: The author notes that colour pickers and design tools are normal parts of CSS work for professionals, and wanted to give beginners that same visual bridge to theme code.
problem: Obsidian offers no interactive way to learn how theme settings map to CSS variables, so beginners must start from a blank theme.css file.
summary: Visual learning studio that teaches Obsidian theme creation through simple controls, a live preview, and generated CSS you export as a standalone theme.
